blocks.size_first: SIZE FIRST: the eye cream is ONE slim tube about 16 cm long and 2 cm wide (15 ml), about as long as an adult hand from the wrist crease to the fingertip and about as wide as one and a half fingers. It is about 8 times as long as it is wide, exactly the proportions in image 1. It is never bigger than the hand holding it.
blocks.product_block: The eye cream is the REAL product in the reference images and it must not change: the top 60% is a soft matte WHITE squeeze tube whose far end is a flat crimped white seal; the bottom 40% is the polished chrome applicator: a smooth silver cylinder a little narrower than the tube, one thin matte BLACK ring band at its end, then a short polished chrome tip that narrows into a waist and flares into a flat round end face with one tiny hole in the centre. The print on the white tube is copied from image 2 exactly: small, thin, elegant black SERIF capitals like a classic book face (never bold, never sans-serif), three short centred lines in the upper part of the tube, each line only about half the tube's width; below them a thin black outlined oval with a black 'HB' monogram inside; below that seven lines of very small black capitals and one tiny volume line near the chrome. The three title lines read BLACK YUJA BEAN, LIFTING AUTO, EYE CREAM and nothing else. Most of the tube is plain white space. No other words anywhere on the tube, no colour, no button, no switch, no light, no gold or rose gold metal, no roller ball.
blocks.cap_on: The matte BLACK cylinder cap is ON: it covers the chrome tip and the black ring, so only the white tube and part of the chrome cylinder show, exactly as in image 3.
blocks.cap_off: The black cap is OFF and nowhere in the frame; the chrome tip is bare and shaped exactly as in image 3.
blocks.hand_block: ONLY one hand enters from the frame edge: Grace's hand exactly as in the hand reference sheet: medium-brown skin, slim fingers, medium-length square natural pink nails with crisp white French tips; a BARE wrist with no bracelet, no watch and no chain; rings exactly as in the sheet: a silver crown-shaped stack ring on the ring finger, a thin GOLD ring with a small clear heart-shaped stone on the middle finger, and a glossy blue silicone band on the THUMB, never on the wrist. Whole wrist visible, a little forearm in a soft cream knit sleeve may show, five fingers, natural knuckles and skin texture. The fingers GRIP the tube: thumb on one side, fingers on the other, on the chrome part.
blocks.face_block: The skin is Grace's, exactly as in the face reference: medium-dark brown skin with real pores and texture, defined arched brows, almond dark-brown eyes, natural lashes, no heavy makeup. Relaxed face, smooth relaxed forehead, no frown.
blocks.no_hand: No hand, arm, fingers or people anywhere in the frame.
blocks.light: Bright soft daylight, clean neutral white balance, never yellow, golden, dark or moody.
blocks.suffix: Vertical 9:16 photo, a single frame from a phone video, realistic textures, sharp focus. Every other item is plain and unbranded. No text, no captions, no watermark, no phone UI, no date stamp.
blocks.omni_head: Recreate image 1 exactly as the first frame: keep its room, light, framing{who} and the eye cream exactly. The eye cream is the real product in images 2 to {sheet}: a matte white tube with black serif print and the black 'HB' oval logo, and a polished chrome applicator with one black ring band and a short chrome tip that flares into a flat round end. Its print must match image 2 letter for letter and colour for colour; its shape and size never change.
blocks.omni_tail: One continuous handheld phone shot, 4 seconds, bright neutral daylight that never changes. The tube never turns, flips, bends or changes size; no second tube appears. No text, no captions, no music, no voice.

shots.words: Okay, watch what happens when I touch the tip of this eye cream.
shots.props: one clear glass coupe (a wide shallow stemmed glass) half full of clear water
shots.still: Close eye-level view of the wooden bathroom counter from the room photo, the sage tiles and round mirror soft and out of focus behind. TWO hands: her LEFT hand enters from the left edge and holds a clear glass coupe half full of clear water by its stem, lifted a little above the counter in the lower half of the frame; that hand has no rings and a bare wrist. TIP POSITION FIRST: the whole eye cream stays OUTSIDE and ABOVE the glass. Her RIGHT hand (the one in the hand reference sheet, with its rings) enters from the top right edge holding the eye cream at a slant from above the right side of the glass, thumb and two fingers pinching the chrome cylinder; only the flat round end of the chrome tip touches the glass, resting ON the RIM (the thin top edge of the bowl) at the right side of the bowl. No part of the tube or tip is inside the bowl, below the rim or near the water. The tip touches only the glass: it is never dipped into the water, and nothing goes into the water. Fine shivering ripples cover the water surface. The tube fills about 45% of the frame height and is never taller than the hand is long. PROPORTIONS, exactly as image 1: the polished chrome part is LONG, about 40% of the whole tube's length (as long as the hand's index finger), a straight chrome cylinder from the white tube down to the thin black ring, then the short flared tip below the ring; the white part is the other 60%. PRINT ORDER from the crimped end down, exactly as image 2 and as the tube in image 4: first the three title lines BLACK YUJA BEAN / LIFTING AUTO / EYE CREAM, then BELOW them the thin black outlined upright oval with the 'HB' monogram inside (never above the title, never without the oval), then the seven tiny ingredient lines, then the volume line. Under the oval only seven very short lines of tiny text, each line about a third of the tube's width, then lots of plain white space; never a long paragraph of text.
shots.motion: In the first half second her right hand lifts the tube a little so the flat round end of the chrome tip comes up and rests ON the RIM of the glass (the thin top edge of the bowl); then the tip stays resting on the rim for the rest of the clip while the water inside trembles: fine, fast ripples shiver across the whole water surface. Her left hand holding the glass by its stem stays still. The tip never goes inside the bowl, below the rim or into the water. No splash, no bubbles. Camera holds, a very slight push-in.
shots.risk: money move: tip against the glass, water trembling
shots.see: Hand holds the tube tip-down; the chrome tip touches the water in a glass coupe on a bathroom counter, rings spread (riskiest, made first)
extra_refs: an earlier frame of this same eye cream: copy its tube print layout and its long chrome part exactly; ignore its water and its scene

shots.words: Hear that? It turns on by itself. Twelve thousand vibrations a minute.
shots.props: the same clear glass coupe of water
shots.still: Top-down macro view straight into the clear glass coupe of water on the wooden counter: the water surface fills most of the frame, the flat round chrome end of the tip touches the middle of the surface, the chrome cylinder and black ring rise toward the top edge, and the hand's fingertips pinch the chrome at the very top edge of the frame. Tight concentric ripple rings already spread from the tip.
shots.motion: The camera slowly pushes in toward the flat chrome tip resting on the rim of the glass until the tip, the rim and the trembling water fill most of the frame. The tip stays resting on the rim the whole time and never goes inside the bowl or into the water; the water inside trembles with fine, fast ripples across its whole surface. Both hands stay still. No splash, no bubbles.
shots.see: Push-in from S1's last frame onto the tip resting on the rim, water trembling

shots.words: Let's be for real, most eye cream is just lotion that ends up on your finger,
shots.still: Close view in front of the pink tiled bathroom from the room photo, soft and out of focus behind. ONE hand enters from the bottom right edge, palm up, ring finger and middle finger raised toward the lens; a smear of ivory-white eye cream sits on the pad of the ring finger, thick and shiny, clearly left over. The hand fills the lower half of the frame.
shots.motion: The thumb slowly rubs the cream on the ring finger pad, spreading the leftover cream across the fingertip; the cream stays on the finger. Camera holds.
shots.see: Fingertip with leftover eye cream, thumb rubs it around (no product)

shots.words: Then your concealer still creases by lunch.
shots.still: Extreme close-up of the left side of Grace's face from the eyebrow down to the top of the cheek, by a bright window: one open eye looking slightly down, the under-eye area in sharp focus with a thin layer of light concealer that has settled into fine creases under the eye. The bridge of the nose touches the frame edge; NO mouth, NO lips and no chin anywhere in the frame. The bright bedroom from the room photo is soft and out of focus at the edge.
shots.motion: Very slow push-in on the creased concealer under the eye; she blinks once, slowly. Nothing else moves.
shots.see: Under-eye close-up, concealer settled into fine creases, slow push-in, she blinks (no mouth)

shots.words: This one has the massage tip built in, so a tiny dot gets worked right in.
shots.still: HAND AND SIDE FIRST: this is her RIGHT eye and her RIGHT hand. She faces the camera, so her right eye, right cheek and right ear are on the LEFT side of the frame. Close-up of the right side of Grace's face from the eyebrow down to the top of the cheek, the pink tiled bathroom soft behind; NO mouth, NO lips and no chin in the frame. Her eye is relaxed, open and looking up a little, fully visible ABOVE the tip. PLACEMENT FIRST: the chrome tip touches the soft under-eye skin BELOW the lower lashes, in the hollow between the bottom of the eye and the top of the cheekbone, about one finger-width below the lower lash line. The tip is never at the level of the eye, never beside the eye, never on the eyelid and never above the eye. ONE hand, her RIGHT hand (the hand in the hand reference sheet, with its rings), comes up from the bottom-LEFT edge holding the eye cream by the chrome cylinder; the tube points DOWN and AWAY from the face toward the bottom-left corner, so the whole tube sits below the eye. Never her left hand, never a hand from the right edge. The FLAT ROUND END of the chrome tip (the end with the tiny hole) presses flat against that under-eye skin, so the end face is hidden against the skin and never faces the camera; only the side of the flared tip, the black ring and the chrome cylinder are seen. A thin sheen of ivory-white cream on the under-eye skin around the tip. Only the chrome part and a little of the white tube show.
shots.motion: The flat end of the chrome tip stays pressed against the under-eye skin below the lower lashes and glides slowly along under the eye from the outer corner toward the inner corner (left to right in the frame), always below the eye, spreading the cream into a thin sheen; the tube keeps pointing down and away from the face, the end face never turns toward the camera. One slow pass, the grip never changes, the eye stays relaxed and open above the tip.
shots.risk: tip on the face under the eye
shots.see: Chrome tip glides under her eye spreading a small dot of cream (no mouth)

shots.words: It's yuja water, black bean and collagen for dry skin.
shots.props: a shallow speckled stone bowl full of shiny black soybeans and one yuja (a small yellow citrus) cut in half beside it
shots.still: Close three-quarter view from above of the grey marble bathroom counter from the room photo, the yellow flowers soft behind. A shallow speckled stone bowl full of shiny black soybeans; the eye cream lies diagonally across the beans with the cap on, its print facing up and readable; a yuja cut in half lies on the counter beside the bowl, juicy yellow flesh up. The tube fills about 55% of the frame width.
shots.motion: The camera barely moves: a tiny, slow handheld drift to the side at the same distance, no push-in and no zoom. The tube lies still on the beans the whole time and never moves; the beans and the yuja stay still.
shots.see: Tube, cap on, lying in a stone bowl of black beans, a cut yuja beside it, tiny camera drift (no push-in)

shots.words: It goes on smile lines and your neck too.
shots.still: Close-up of the right side of Grace's neck from just under the jawline down to the collarbone, her chin lifted slightly; NO mouth, NO lips and no eyes in the frame. Her braids are swept behind her shoulder. ONE hand enters from the bottom left edge holding the eye cream by the chrome cylinder; the flat chrome tip rests on the side of the neck with a small sheen of cream. The pink tiled bathroom is soft behind.
shots.motion: The chrome tip glides slowly upward along the side of the neck toward the jawline, one smooth pass; the grip never changes. The head stays still.
shots.see: Tip glides up the side of her neck toward the jaw (no mouth)

shots.words: People say that cool metal tip makes plain eye cream feel boring.
shots.still: Close view of the cream vanity top in the bright bedroom from the room photo, the ornate gold mirror and small pine plant soft behind. The eye cream stands upright in a small clear glass tumbler, chrome tip pointing UP, white crimped end down inside the glass, print facing the lens. The tube fills about 50% of the frame height; the tumbler is about a third as tall as the tube.
shots.motion: Slow camera arc a little to the right around the tumbler; the tube and glass stay still.
shots.see: Tube standing tip-up in a small glass tumbler on a bedroom vanity, slow camera arc

shots.words: Cold weather dries out under eyes, so grab one for you and one for your mom's stocking.
shots.still: Close view of the red and white knit Christmas stockings hanging on the stone fireplace from the room photo. ONE hand enters from the right edge holding the eye cream with the cap on, white tube up, print facing the lens, and lowers it into the open top of one red stocking; half the tube is already inside the stocking. Exactly one eye cream in the frame.
shots.motion: The hand slowly lowers the tube a little further into the stocking and lets go, leaving the white top and print showing above the cuff; the hand leaves the frame to the right. The stockings sway very slightly.
shots.see: Hand drops ONE capped tube into a red Christmas stocking on the fireplace

shots.words: I linked it in the orange cart for you.
shots.props: a small plain white ceramic dish
shots.still: Close view of the wooden vanity top against the deep teal wall from the room photo, the gold wall lamp soft behind. ONE eye cream lies on a small plain white ceramic dish, cap off, chrome tip pointing to the right, print facing up and readable. The tube fills about 60% of the frame width. Exactly one tube.
shots.motion: The camera barely moves: a tiny, slow handheld drift to the side at the same distance, no push-in and no zoom. The tube lies flat on the dish the whole time: it never lifts, tilts, stands up, rolls or moves at all.
shots.see: End: ONE tube on a small white dish on a vanity by a teal wall, tiny camera drift (no push-in)
